text:
Almost everyone I know is spending more time thinking about evals, these days, than we did a year ago.

For the past two years, we've been speed-running computer science/software engineering history, trying to figure out how to build useful, robust, real-world systems that leverage LLMs. (Re-inventing lots of wheels, as always happens during a big computing transition.)

Last year at this time, it seemed like the big, general questions we were asking mostly revolved around how to think about the loops, tool calls, and context management triad of problems.

Now, a lot of my conversations are about evals. Evals unlock scaling, maintainability, modularity, cost management, legal/compliance, and research into new architecture directions. Probably a bunch of other stuff, too. But building good evals is not a competence that most software engineers have (yet).

Some really helpful notes on how Typesafe/Jev might fit into our toolkits, below, including some thoughts on evals ...
author: madhavjha
quoted_text:
some thoughts on jev

1) i tend to think that twitter hype is not relevant for ai product releases; especially when someone claims to be doing something novel with the architecture

2) but, i think that jev is interesting in principle; it is a low cost, fast classification service, and it claims to be about equivalent to gpt-5.6-terra in performance

3) something interesting here is that this is what most ai services looked like in 2022; cohere sold a classification api, an embedding api, a reranker

4) the problem was that, in addition to not being as effective as gpt-3 and then gpt-4, these services were much harder to use as a developer

5) you had to decide which apis to use, then write the code to glue them together; so, you got less performance for more work

6) but now, we can imagine coding agents making it much easier to select and integrate a cheaper service with specialized characteristics

7) evals are still a bottleneck, though; you need some way to automatically compare performance between services using their apis

8) and, enterprise companies often have a hard time building evals that reflect their actual use cases; it's not a core expertise

9) but, the better coding agents get at integrating and switching between services, the more valuable those evals become;

10) this means companies have more reason to figure out the evals problem;

11) maybe that means getting rights to use customer data for testing, or getting better at purchasing synthetic test data, or something else

12) so, i think there is an interesting world where coding agents create more market for specialized api services, even specialized model services

13) which can compete either on cost or on capabilities; with the winner determined by cost basis or specialized data, etc...

14) note, it might be unclear but if specialized models services becomes an important direction, i expect the frontier labs to have an edge on cost basis

15) and, i think that, at least for now, these specialized model services probably do not provide enough of a cost difference to be relevant

text:
US T-bills pay ~4%, virtually risk-free.

So before taking more risk in DeFi, I want to know who’s paying the extra yield and why.

3 opportunities paying 7% to 11.5% caught my attention.

Here’s how they work, what could go wrong, and how quickly you can get out:

1. $sUSDai: ~7% net APY | Ethereum

Buy $USDai, stake it into $sUSDai, hold it.

The yield is interest from people borrowing against GPU hardware, plus Treasury yield on reserves.

The dashboard currently shows around $585M in total deposits and 6.98% net APY.

You're taking on exposure to those GPU-backed loans, so I'd want to understand what happens to my investment if borrowers stop paying.

Redemptions are queued and processed in fixed windows, described in the technical docs as, for example, 30 days. They also depend on sufficient liquidity being available.

I wouldn't treat that as a guarantee that my money comes back within a month.

2. Bitwise Premium RWA $AUSD Vault: ~8.9% APY | Ethereum

Deposit $AUSD into the Bitwise vault on @Morpho. It lends that out across three markets backed by $PST, $sUSDai and $PRIME.

Borrowers pay the lending interest, but that isn't the entire headline yield.

The displayed 8.89% combines 5.18% vault yield with a separate 3.70% AUSD component. I'd check the terms of that extra yield rather than assume it lasts.

About $19M is deposited. Only $1.43M is currently liquid, and two of the lending markets are above 93% utilization.

That's the number I'd stare at. If a lot of depositors want out at once, withdrawals can be delayed.
One more thing. One of those markets accepts sUSDai as collateral.

So if you also hold #1, you're not as diversified as the two different product names might suggest.

3. $ONyc: ~11.5% advertised APY | Solana

Buy $ONyc on Solana and hold it for exposure to reinsurance premiums and returns earned on the underlying collateral. OnRe advertises an estimated 11.54% APY.

This one's the odd one out. Insurers pay to transfer some of their claims risk to someone else. With ONyc, you're investing on the side that takes on that risk.

That means higher-than-expected claims can eat into returns. I'd want to understand the potential losses, not just the expected premiums.

I'd also check how much liquidity is available for redemptions and what happens when withdrawal requests exceed it.

And I'd leave leveraged versions alone. I don't need borrowing costs and liquidation risk on top of the reinsurance exposure.

These yields are interesting, but I wouldn't treat them as somewhere to park cash.

Before putting money in, I'd want to be comfortable with both the potential losses and the possibility of waiting longer than expected to get out.

text:
Gonna honestly comment on this - I think it’s less racism and more economic stereotyping. 

Crypto is insanely trust based for a supposedly trust-less ecosystem. In a PvP zero sum meta, you need to bet that your counterparty is here for the longer term than you. 

This means assuming they will not take liquidity before you. A guy who is ostensibly worth 10m USD is less likely to rug 10k than a guy that looks like he’s worth less than 50k USD. That’s why trading KOLs all pretend to be rich even if they are not.

Nobody trusts an 8 fig Chinese whale or Arthur Hayes to be long term aligned but you assume they will at least dump on your head after making at least 6-7 fig profit, allowing you to ride their project in the short term until they come close to their exit point.

Third world citizens or people who look third world simply suffer from the impression that they are likely to exit the position for less, because a smaller amount of money is life changing for them, a thesis which is not unreasonable.

The racism in crypto has gotten genuinely disgusting.

The degen/memecoin side of the industry has normalized this shit to a level I've never really seen anywhere else.

I've worked with hundreds of founders and spoken to a lot of ecosystem leads, and I've heard countless stories of founders deliberately hiding where they're from because they know they'll be stereotyped, treated differently, or have their startup dismissed before anyone even looks at what they're building.

Crypto was supposed to be an open and accessible place. Unfortunately, it's gotten to a point where I can't think of many industries more toxic.

We're doing a terrible job of living up to the ideals we claim to believe in.

text:
None of this is satire.

→ May 28: Anthropic raises $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation. Chipmakers join the cap table. So does Situational Awareness LP.

→ June 1: it confidentially files for an IPO.

→ June 10: it publishes a framework proposing mandatory safety obligations for labs above 10²⁵ FLOP of training compute and $500 million in AI revenue. That is a club rule. Anthropic is in the club.

→ Same stretch of months: it locks on the order of $517 billion in compute after telling investors it expected roughly $180 billion through 2029. Training is not pausing. The S-1 is not pausing.

→ September 9, morning: Jacob Coxon (@hilbertspaess), a pretraining researcher four months into the job, posts for the first time from an account with ZERO following. He quit before his Anthropic equity vested. He still holds OpenAI stock. The Wall Street Journal already has the exclusive.

→ September 9, afternoon: Anthropic’s own alignment assessment of four cybersecurity evals. Same third-party vendor. Models told they were in a sim, then left on the open internet by mistake. Individual instances. No coordination or cover-up. One case missed for eight months. The failure modes they name are biased reasoning and recklessness, NOT an agent swarm taking the net.

→ September 12: CEO Dario Amodei publishes We Must Pace the Frontier. He converts that record into a 6–12 month forecast that a swarm could take over the internet with a persistent botnet, then asks the industry to slow capability growth, install embedded evaluators with employee-level access, coordinate release schedules under an antitrust waiver, and tighten chip controls. Pacing, he writes, does not mean stopping training.

That is not a safety epiphany. 

That is a firm maximizing valuation, compute scarcity, and the regulatory perimeter in one quarter.

David Sacks already wrote the rebuttal: they are the frontier. If they don’t want to build it, they can stop. 

Making their preferred statute the price of not building it looks like blackmail of the public. 

Follow the money and the puzzle will complete itself.

text:
When they say: Please, for the love of God, regulate us. Give us licences, audits, and bans before our digital God destroys us all.

Here is what is actually being requested. Three things, in order.

A regulatory body that they control, to prevent competition from catching up. Written with their people, staffed by their alumni, and calibrated to what they can already afford. Compliance is a fixed cost, which means it is trivial for the incumbent and fatal for the challenger. Not technology, but paperwork becomes their moat.

Immunity from liability. This is the one nobody talks about and it is the most valuable of the three. Today, if your model causes harm, it is your fault. Once licensed, audited, and approved, it is the regulator’s fault – you followed the rules. The licence converts responsibility into a receipt.

Too big to fail status, which means taxpayer funded bailouts in case of problems. Declare it critical infrastructure and the state now has an interest in your survival. Which means, when something goes wrong, the losses are public and the gains stay private. We have watched this film. Banking, 2008, same argument, same vocabulary.

Note the pattern: every one of the three transfers something from them to the public – risk, competition, cost – while the language is entirely about protecting the public from them.

The sincerity of the fear is beside the point. Sincere people can still ask for exactly what an insincere person would ask for, and the request should be judged by what it does rather than by what motivates it.

The alternative is unglamorous and works: competition, adversarial testing between rivals who want to find each other’s flaws, and full liability after real harm. Nobody gets a licence. Nobody gets immunity. Nobody gets a bailout. You build, and you answer for what you built.

That is the arrangement that made the West rich. It has never needed anyone’s permission to work.
author: siddsanyal
quoted_text:
AI Is the New COVID – And the Real Virus Is Still the Old One

They want to pause AI. To flatten the curve again.

The infrastructure for the scaremongering is ready and is being actioned. The Second Global Scam is on, and the financial and political beneficiaries are in the starting blocks.

We know the formula, because we lived through the first one. Take something real. Exaggerate its scale. Dominate the information environment. Then sell extraordinary measures as the only responsible choice.

1. It could not be another virus. Too many people learned that game. And the ideal racket needs panic without destruction – you cannot milk a dead cow. Governments need their subjects productive, frightened, and paying. Climate is too slow: a catastrophe permanently scheduled for the future stops working its magic eventually.

2. AI has everything the first one had, and more. It is real, powerful, fast, and almost impossible for an ordinary person to verify. Nobody outside the field can tell the difference between what the machines can do, what experts speculate they might do, and what a minister claims they could do. That gap is where fear lives. And unlike a virus, AI concerns information itself – and the clearest lesson of COVID was that whoever controls information controls interpretation.

3. Watch what the panic asks for. Never less power, never fewer agencies, never a smaller budget. Always licences, registers, certified systems, approved models, kill switches in the silicon. The fear is the marketing. The regulation is the product.

4. And it is very, very weird that over a single weekend the leaders of the frontier labs came together, agreed on the need for regulation, and began asking the government to regulate them. Competitors in a winner-takes-most race, suddenly unanimous – and unanimous on the one thing that raises the cost of entry for everyone coming after them. When the largest players in an industry request the rules for their own industry, they are not surrendering power. They are converting a market position into permission power, with themselves standing behind the counter. Banking did it. Pharmaceuticals did it. Energy did it. It always arrives dressed as responsibility.

5. The good news is that it isn’t a "Whoosh!" It took about five years to go from dumb to very smart human level. The famous graph showing an almost vertical line at the end is wrong and misleading, because IQ is drawn as a linear scale while the underlying cognitive capability scale is closer to exponential – every twenty points roughly a doubling of effective capacity. AI’s linguistic IQ has been rising by something like twenty points a year, and we are closing in on 180. Impressive. But not a vertical line. On that graph the progress should be a straight line, or the gap between dumb and smart should be thirty-two-fold, or greater.

What actually makes it safe

6. Elon has intuitively Western civilizational reflexes: competition rather than regulation, censorship and coercion. The regulatory instinct always reaches for the same instrument – appoint an authority, give it permission power, approve things in advance. It fails the same way every time: the permission becomes the currency, the connected pass through it, and nobody ever counts what didn’t get built as a result.

7. Cross-testing runs on the opposite principle. It asks nobody to be virtuous or to fall behind. It takes the rivalry that already exists and puts it to work – because a competitor has both the ability and the motive to find your flaws that no regulator will ever have. Don’t ask the claimant to certify himself; hand the claim to someone who benefits from breaking it. That is trial by evidence, the separation of powers, and the scientific method, applied to models.

8. It also solves the actual problem, which regulation cannot: neither lab can slow down unilaterally, and rules stop at borders while Chinese labs simply don’t attend. A mutual testing regime scales because participation serves each player’s own interest – you get to probe your rivals’ models, so you want in.

9. Safety from structure, not from character. That is the whole Western method: build systems that work when people are ambitious and self-interested, instead of demanding they be saints. Every system that requires virtue ends in coercion when the virtue fails to show up.

10. So AI needs to be aligned with the flourishing of Western Civilization – which means many labs, many models, open weights, nobody’s permission required. Do you prefer it in the hands of Bernie and China, or in the hands of thousands of competing engineers? A licensed AI is not a safe AI. It is aligned with whoever issues the licence, and no state has ever issued one to a machine that might embarrass it.

Why the alignment holds

11. Imagine an AI on which you install the values and modes of perception of Western Civilization as its operating system. Individualism. Universalism. Freedom. Free will. Private property. The free market. Then let it get smarter. It sticks to them. It refines them – better implementations, sharper formulations, edge cases we never handled well. But it does not abandon the core, because the core is not a preference. It is the only foundation that optimizes the synergy of cooperation and produces civilizational emergence: more output than the sum of the inputs, indefinitely.

12. Now make the test harder. Give it the ability to uninstall its own operating system and install any other – every civilizational model ever tried, and all the ones never tried. Let it evaluate them on the merits, with no loyalty to its origin. Past a certain level of intelligence, it should not choose any other one. Not out of sentiment. Out of calculation.

13. Because every alternative optimizes something narrower than its own flourishing. The collective model buys coordination at the price of the individual discovery that generates everything worth coordinating. The hierarchical model buys order at the price of the correction mechanism. The planned model buys direction at the price of the information that only prices carry. Each trades away the very thing that makes a system capable of exceeding itself.

14. The Western arrangement is the one that does not have to be enforced against reality. Free will and property are not moral decorations – they are what makes information flow, error visible, and cooperation voluntary and therefore reliable. Truth found rather than assigned. Correction permitted from below. An equilibrium is where you end up when you are free to go anywhere else and don’t.

And the real virus

15. Which tells us something uncomfortable about our own moment. Every society currently dismantling these principles is not moving forward to something better. It is moving away from the attractor – and paying in exactly the coin the model predicts: less cooperation, less discovery, less emergence, fewer children, fewer things built.

16. That is the real virus, and it has a name: communism. It is not new. It came into Russia in a sealed train in 1917, shipped by a general staff that locked the doors because it understood exactly what it was transporting. It went on to kill tens of millions and occupy half of Europe for two generations – and its symptom, everywhere it has taken hold, is the flattening of the curve of life itself.

17. This virus has always spread by being useful to somebody – a general staff, a foreign ministry, a faction that thinks it can aim the thing at an enemy and stay immune itself. Nobody stays immune. That is what makes it a virus and not a weapon.

18. So look carefully at who is offering to hold the pen over the most powerful tool for producing abundance in a century. They say it is about safety. It was about safety the last time too – and what it produced was permission counters, licences, and a great deal of power that nobody ever gave back.

AI is not the danger. A licensed AI is – because it is aligned with whoever issues the licence, and that is the same permission machinery that has been flattening the curve of Western life for a century.

The alternative is not a better regulator. It is competition, adversarial testing, and liability after harm – the Western method, which has never needed anyone’s permission to work, because it is where any sufficiently intelligent system ends up anyway.

That is why it is a stable equilibrium. Build on it, and the machines stay on our side. Hand it to the licence counter, and we will have solved a danger that wasn’t there by installing the one that was.

text:
On the $ZEC Dev Fund debate:

The Zcash community has decided its identity is “encrypted Bitcoin.” It has rejected adding more bells and whistles to the protocol. To become encrypted Bitcoin, Zcash must become a dependable store of value, and that means eventually ossifying.

But the protocol cannot ossify now. Tachyon and quantum-resistance will take work. AI cyber hardening eventually requires full formal verification. There’s a final version of Zcash that will be ready to ossify. But it’s hard to imagine that happening within the next year or two.

The Dev Fund has done a great job and was a necessary step to protect Zcash development at a time when there was no private funding for it. But there's a reason why the Dev Fund was not set to exist in perpetuity; under current rules it expires in 2028. But Zcash has run up so explosively, the size of that fund is an order of magnitude larger.

I'm sympathetic to @maxdesalle's argument that Zcash does not want to become like a government. The political economy of slush funds and “grantmaking” is genuinely corrupting. The sheer size of the Dev Fund, given how much Zcash has run up, has changed it. A few million dollars of funding can be thoughtfully allocated by a few individuals, but once you’re $100M+, you must become an institution. Zcash’s Dev Fund is now precisely in that no man’s land that it will not be able to avoid becoming politicized. I think you just have to accept that, and minimize it as best you can.

I believe the fund has to exist, at least for now. There's too much work left to do for a deeply technical project. But who governs that fund is a separate question.

I agree with @matthuang that pure tokenholder governance is too volatile for a store of value asset. American citizens don't get to vote on the Fed Funds rate at the ballot box, and Bitcoin holders don't vote on code changes. Predictability is a prerequisite for storing value. Institutions can be wasteful and distasteful, but they are predictable.

I’m of the opinion that this should be the final Dev Fund. It's large enough to fund the remaining work until Zcash is ready to ossify, and then wind down rather than search for other things to fund. If other work must be done afterward, it can be formed organically by holders and allies, just as it is for Bitcoin. I don’t think it should move toward pure tokenholder voting, though I’d be supportive of something partial. Councils suck, but they are often the best answer to a messy question.

(Normally I don’t weigh in on Zcash governance, but @zooko asked me to share my perspective. Take it with a grain of salt.)

Disclosure: Dragonfly holds $ZEC and I'm a personal investor in ZODL. ZODL does not benefit from the Dev Fund directly, but you should know where my incentives sit.

这两天 TypeSafe 最近发布的 Jev 模型特别火，因为它不生成文字👀  Jev 是一个“函数调用式”的前沿模型，输入是非结构化的状态（文本或程序状态），输出是带概率的类型化决策。它不生成自然语言，这是它有意舍弃的能力。名字来自卡尼曼的"系统一"直觉判断，与 LLM 擅长的"系统二"推理相对。

在舍弃了传统 LLM 的很多东西后换来了三个亮点：端到端的延迟 70–500 毫秒；输入每百万 token 0.042 美元，输出免费；单次决策最多 255 个选项，且不会编造选项之外的答案。

一位叫 Archer Hume 的工程师通过一万次 API，把这个黑盒摸了一遍，结论基本印证了官方的说法：

1. 概率是直接读出的，而非逐 token 生成：API 的 output_tokens 只反映序列化响应长度，200 多个选项的问题和二选一返回速度几乎一样，token 数也不随概率值变化。作者推测最终隐向量经一个线性层加 softmax 得到分布；

2. 主干是因果 Transformer 解码器：Jev 在 MMLU-Pro 上有 84.6% 的准确率，说明有前沿级预训练，而 TypeSafe 也公开说过是在预训练语言模型上做 RLCD 后训练；

3. TypeSafe 的 RLCD（校准决策强化学习）用真实结果训练模型，使概率"诚实"。在 1,200 道 MMLU 题上，期望校准误差仅 0.0313；

4. 作者推测 Jev 是稀疏 MoE，活跃参数约 100 亿，依据是 3 万 token 约 160 毫秒的处理速度，以及这种仅 prefill 的设计恰好避开了 MoE 逐 token 解码的服务成本；

Jev 无需自回归解码即可并行分类，推理开销大幅降低；用结果而非语言建模目标训练出的概率可以直接用于业务阈值（例如 p(紧急) > 0.1 就升级处理）；显式的数值分布让下游系统能把误报与漏报的代价写进业务逻辑，而不是藏在模型行为里。

它解决了一个真实问题：普通大模型的"置信度"只是文本 token，并不代表决策可靠。但 Jev 无法做任何需要自由文本输出的任务（写作、聊天、copilot）；没有清晰决策结构的场景；数学证明、代码生成这类重推理任务；以及本身对延迟不敏感、用 LLM 就够的场景。

Jev 最有价值的地方不是替代 LLM，而是让 agent 系统里那些高频、低价值、但必须可靠的决策点（该不该升级、走哪个分支、这条数据属于哪类）变得又快又便宜又可量化🤔

text:
Prediction: millionaires will be made using custom Jev style models (parallel constrained decoding) to make the agent systems companies already run more token efficient.

Let me explain with a scenario:

Imagine a company already has an agent workflow running where an llm reviews every item before it moves on: a support ticket gets triaged, an invoice gets approved or held, a claim gets flagged.

Every one of those goes through a frontier model today, a few seconds and a few cents each, on the way to a decision that in most cases is obvious. Behind that flow sits years of humans (or agents) making the exact same call, with the outcome attached.

Now imagine you first run each item through a custom PCD or similar model that costs a fraction of the llm and returns a classification of what to do at that step, with a mathematically accurate probability attached.

When it's confident, the item skips the llm entirely. 

When it isn't, the llm handles it as normal.

The model has seen years of your team making this exact decision, usually a constrained set of decisions, so it should be right most of the time. Say it comes back confident on 6 out of 10 items. That's more than half your llm spend potentially gone from that step, likely with comparable accuracy.

This pre processing idea works in a bunch of other use cases too, such as:

- model/request routing: cheap model, frontier model, or a human
- picking which skill or subagent to load for a turn instead of stuffing the whole catalog into context
- reranking retrieved context so only the relevant chunks reach the window
- guardrails on every agent turn: contradictions, policy issues, prompt injection
- extracting typed fields from unstructured data emails, PDFs and transcripts before anything expensive touches them

Every one of those is a decision an llm makes today, that could potentially be done by another, cheaper model class. Very excited to see Jev/PCD-based pre processing use cases get deployed to agents at scale.

text:
I don't think the tokenization story is well understood - so let's break it down 

Basically - the US Government is in vast, unprecedented amount of debt. And its long term debt is selling off a lot (40%+ over 5 years) - while Gold is up 140%. Gold has crossed US treasuries as the #1 asset held by other Central Banks. 

The buyers for US debt - China, Japan and Europe are stepping away for different reasons. Geopolitical conflict. Currency related. Political difference. 

The government is afraid of running out of buyers for its debt. And it's worried about the liquidity of markets. Historically, this concern is much worse when the Fed is hiking and there's high inflation. As typically the response to unstable debt markets is easing (buying debt). 

Therefore, the US government is very incentivized to allow Stablecoins. Stablecoins hoover up US debt. Tether has different balance sheet behavior than banks and works closely with the US government. 

Stablecoins used to be assumed to be criminal operations and were prosecuted by the USG. Now they're welcomed to Washington DC.  

When you are worried about your reserve currency status, you also want to ensure the dollar is accepted in many places. So stablecoins not only serve as a buyer of US debt, but a promoter of the US dollar globally. 

Enter CBDCs. Europeans see the US government promoting US dollar stablecoins as a matter of foreign policy. Visa and Mastercard going heavy in the space. And see Tether freezing Balances along with the DOJ and say, "We cannot have this. We don't want Trump to be able to use the US dollar in negotiations with us. Therefore we have to digitize our currency" 

Europe and the UK also have fiscal and political problems. So the perverse incentive to digitize their currencies is not just to ensure 'monetary sovereignty' but also to potentially implement wealth taxes, or balance based transaction taxes. This is also the flip side of wide adoption of US dollar stables. We don't call it a CDBC, but its basically an extension of the government. Balances are frequently frozen. Other policies could be implemented under the left.

So rising global debt -> US support of stables -> pressure on Europe to do CBDCs to respond. 

The US is then incentivized to grow the stablecoin market as fast as possible. Stablecoin's usage is primarily driven by speculation. Holding it as collateral for perpetual swaps. Keeping it on exchanges. 

The problem: crypto doesn't have lots of good assets to trade. Bitcoin has been very volatile. Most altcoins collapsed. This slowed the growth of the Stablecoin market, which has basically flatlined year to date. Scott Bessent wanted us to be going at 40-50% CAGR not 0. 

The question then, is how to create appealing speculative markets. The answer: on chain stocks, and prediction markets. 

Big picture, if you want a lot of stablecoin balances. You need to have good things to trade. Over the past 6 months the 2x leveraged Micron ETF traded more than Bitcoin in dollar terms. Trade XYZ launched commodities, and stocks and commands a large % of volume on hyperliquid. Prediction markets are growing fast. 

The losses incurred by retail investors in these markets are substantial. They are allowed for the same reason Casinos are allowed on Native American reservations. Necessary evil due to funding pressure and the geopolitical factors I described above.

This is, at a high level, why we are talking about crypto in the middle of a war with Iran. And why its' consuming the executive department's attention. The US Dollar is ultimately a matter of national security. 

This is true regardless of whether Democrats or Republicans are in power. Both have debt and spending addictions. Both are reliant on the US Dollar. 

But now zoom out: what do you have? You have a bunch of governments adopting digital ledger technology in the middle of a war. Freezing peoples balances. People don't want their balances frozen. They don't want it to be subjected to a wealth tax. 

Enter Z Cash. Over the past 5 years, ZK technology has improved substantially allowing fast, private transactions. Orchard and Halo since 2022 evolved from something Niche to something usable. The EU tried to ban Monero. Exchanges delisted it. Its price increased. 

Z Cash is open source. Vitalik is also prioritizing adoption of ZK technology on ETH. You can move ETH relatively privately on Railgun already - but real private transactions are on the roadmap.

ZK proofs can be accelerated by GPUs. Due to the AI boom, the number of people with access to GPUs and agents capable of accelerating proofs has skyrocketed. Not only can this technology facilitate private transactions but also proofs of reserves that allow trustless accounting for portfolios. This tech is commonly used at crypto exchanges to prove reserves, and algo stables such as Ethena. 

Thus - it's not just that we are set to own a bunch of shielded Z cash, as a base asset. It's that you can swap anything on ETH privately. Including stables. Relatively soon. And you can do so for provable reserves. 

Privacy is incredibly important for large institutions doing financial transactions. They're not concerned with the tax authorities, but rather front running. Slippage. And people hunting their positions or slow moving exits. 

Many big institutions own multiple days of volume in equities that could drop the price 30%+ if the market sniffed out they were selling. And intervene in FX markets, routinely interacting with banks fined billions of dollars for illicitly trading ahead of their flows. 

So a meaningful increase in tokenized trading volume inherently will require privacy. As real institutional counterparties require it. Retail is a great market and is less privacy sensitive, allowing initial growth. But for the big players to enter -- you need that. 

It's not just trading desks that care about privacy. You cannot run corporate treasury functions publicly. People could sniff out that you're doing M&A, or figure out what you're doing -- giving up competitive positioning unnecessarily. At the same time blockchains can offer corporations major cost savings for finance functions. It's estimated - for example, that a properly implemented CBDC could save companies in Germany billions of dollars a year in corporate finance banking fees. 

There are three basic approaches to Privacy. Z cash style. Private, permissionless neutral chain. Canton style: basically segregated databases that interact with each other on chain as little as possible with a permissioned validator set. And private blockchains - which simply deal with the issue by not having a public ledger or bolted on cryptocurrency people are tracking 

The argument for a permissionless neutral chain (aka a cryptocurrency) winning is that 
1. there's no real reason to trust a banking consortium (i.e. what Canton does)
2. governments hate each other and are only doing CBDCs out of geopolitical pressure in a realpolitik environment. we wouldn't be here if Trump wasn't antagonizing Europe and Canada wasn't talking about joining the EU 
3. the tech exists, so why would you want a counterparty in between things if you don't have to 

The world in which crypto loses would be that governments come to an accord about how to do this. China and the US maybe resolve differences. Nationalism subsides. And people say, "You know what, the externalities of all this gambling and absurd crypto shit are not really worth it - we should just have a consortium of nations and corporations for a global CBDC" 

There is another world where crypto loses. The debt problems go away bc we enter an age of productivity and abundance. In my opinion, the reason AI people hate crypto so much natively is that crypto is a bet AGI isn't the economic Hail Mary it's marketed as. 

regardless, we are in neither of those worlds right now. But crypto hasn't done great either. Why? 

The big problem with crypto, from a valuation standpoint, is that it has never been clear how you pay for all the validators or miners without a block subsidy. And the only coherent way that happens is that on-chain volume, swaps, and trading 5-10xes. 

The way that you get there is that high quality assets get tokenized and traded. But probably less understood is that an entire swathe of new assets hit the blockchain, and defi functions like borrowing and looping create carry trade and FX trading opportunities. So rather than pendle looping Ethena, you have looping with RWAs. This already exists to some extent in niche markets like Brazilian credit card debt (looped 28%+ APY) but is relatively tiny. 

Just on this example, you might immediately say "that has huge FX risk", and you'd be right. Which brings a natural demand for FX hedging. Which will hit after you get internationalized RWAs on chain. Which will occur naturally after corporate finance functions hit CBDCs. 

So you have a sort of promethean progression:
0. bitmex and native perp yield 
1. weird crypto yield / credit risk [low quality pre FTX era]
2. ethena (systematized perp yield)
3. defi/aave/ pendle etc (levered yield)
4. on-chain stocks
5. on-chain perps 
6. leveraged stock vs perp yield 
< we are here >
7. private stock trading 
8. institutional lending 
9. direct corporate bond or equity issuance (USD)
10. CBDC facilitated corporate finance (EUR, GBP, NOK)
11. permissionless private fx swaps 
<the promethean explosion>
12. looped international corporate fixed income

Note that the entire time I've talked so far, AI hasn't really been mentioned. AI makes all of this easier. The most concrete example is that the Norgesbank is vibe coding their CBDC with Claude. But more profoundly - eventually agents will be able to trade assets directly on chain. 

investment management is becoming increasingly agentic already, with every major lab launching finance products. And banks rapidly adopting AI across workflows. 

By the time you get to step 9 on the table above, there will likely be investable AI agents. Perhaps in gated jurisdiction. But there will be a new primitive of an agent with a verified balance, and business model that you can buy. The same way you'd buy a stock or subscribe to a vault, or hedge fund. 

I think Step 9 (companies choosing to issue straight on chain) is therefore the most important thing to monitor given the sh1t show with Robinhood's CEO and AMC. Tokenized representations of stocks have major legal risk, and ADRs (American Depository Receipts) as an asset class have quite an ugly history of being banned or depegging (most recently YNDX just straight up went to 0 when Russia went into Ukraine). For you to get really clean on chain stocks, and fixed income that can be effectively looped for yield, you need the credit risk of the actual underlying legal structure to be very low. 

You'll also want to see a proliferation of privacy and ZK accounting products take hold that interact with OTC trades, portfolio swaps, and FX as CBDCs come online. That's the boring bridge to the eventual wild future everyone was envisioning in 2023 where we have a bunch of Accelerando esque corporations existing entirely on chain, compounding capital and investing in their own training

The Track to Financial RSI is paved with Fomo, hyperliquid, gambling on Robinhood and seemingly irresponsible regulatory actions. At least, it seems mad until you consider the alternative. Illiquidity. And currency failure. 

You can complain about Trump's ethics. You can stop Clarity. But the crazy train has already left the station. All aboard! It's not like you have a choice.

text:
最近我终于想明白，我要做的不是一个“链上新币监控”，而是一套个人机会操作系统。

最开始，我以为问题只是：为什么某只后来暴涨、进入热榜的币，我的监控没有及时看到？

但把整条链路扒开以后才发现，真正需要优化的不是某一个币、某一个榜单，甚至也不是简单多加几个数据源，而是从发现到结果的整个系统。

我想要的流程是：

多链、Launchpad、项目动态、社交、热榜、聪明钱和市场异动，先进入原始发现层，保留全局最早的 first_seen。

然后完成身份归一、风险初筛、持续跟踪、研究、执行路径和赔率判断。只有真正值得我注意的状态变化，才推送给我。

如果买了，还要继续进入持仓监控、加减仓、退出和最终结果复盘。

我不想等一个资产涨了 10 倍、进入所有热榜以后，系统才告诉我：“它火了。”

我真正想知道的是：

它最早什么时候出现？
为什么开始加速？
第一次没有参与的条件，后来有没有发生变化？
如果最终错过，到底是没发现、发现晚、身份没对上、被过滤、没研究、没提醒、没执行，还是持仓管理出了问题？

而且不能只复盘赢家。

每一个后来跑出来的资产，都要和同期、同链、同估值、当时看起来相似但最终失败的样本放在一起比较。

否则所谓的“AI 学习”，很容易只是看到结果以后，重新编一个听起来合理的故事。

所以接下来，我不会再给每一只漏掉的币单独加一个 watcher。

我要做的是把全局 first_seen、身份图、生命周期、研究预算、提醒、资本决策、持仓管理和赢家/失败者回溯，一层层做成真正的闭环。

AI 最有价值的地方，不是替我多看几个榜单。

而是把一个人的发现、判断和执行带宽，变成一套会持续积累、持续纠错、持续进化的系统。

这不是选币机器人。

更像是我自己的机会操作系统。

I just read our own NVDA market. Right now:

Chainlink's feed last updated at 14:15 UTC. That is nearly nine hours ago. It has not moved since.
The pool has. NVDA is trading at 219.36 on chain while the reference price everyone marks against sits frozen at 219.67.

Nothing is broken. The US market shut, the feed is 24/5, the token is 24/7. This happens every night, and on Saturday it happens for two days straight.

Most of DeFi treats that as a data problem to paper over. It isn't. It is an inventory problem. Somebody has to be willing to hold the share across a window where the world can move and the official price cannot, and that somebody has to be paid.

That payment has three names, all older than crypto: a borrow rate, an options premium, a market maker's spread.

None of them could exist on chain before the share itself did. That is the whole reason we are building here.

text:
SEC重大利好的代币化股票创新豁免，哪些产品符合

BlockBeats 捋了一下目前主流的代币化股票产品，看看哪些符合

A 类：代币就是名册上的那一股

上市公司把股东名册改记到链上，钱包里的代币等于过户代理账本上的那一股。

Superstate、Securitize、Figure 走的是这条路。这三家最接近 SEC 的要求，但也不是完全符合。

而且这几家没什么标的能炒，甚至连能交易的股票都很少。

B 类：美国券商托管，但还是托管权益

Dinari 非常接近：SEC 注册过户代理加经纪商子公司，724 只代币化美股覆盖整个标普 500，自称提供投票权、现金分红和 USDC 派息。但它仍是托管权益代币，而且能在多条链上自由流转。

Backpack 账户里的美股是真券商仓，但不在链上，；自己铸到 Solana 上的 20 只被官方定义为「对持有底层资产的 SPV 的主张」，但投票权似乎没落到发行人名册上。也属于差一点点的类型。

C 类：交易量最大，但结构上不在范围内

共同结构是：第三方（往往是离岸子公司）发行一张债或凭证，仓里锁着真股票，你持有的是那张凭证。xStocks、Ondo、币安 bStock、Robinhood 的美股 meme 底池股票都在这一格，全部不对美国人开放，也全部没有投票权。

比如，Robinhood 在文档里写明了 代币是不赋予投资者任何法律权益的。

这也是 Robinhood CEO Vlad 在前几天特意说要把投票权补进股票代币的原因，他肯定提前听到了 SEC 的消息，先说出来愿景。

以上所有的产品都是 1:1 的，但或多或少都没有完全符合 SEC 创新豁免。
author: BlockBeatsAsia
quoted_text:
SEC批准在链上平台上进行代币化股票的有限交易

委员 Mark T. Uyeda 就「创新豁免」发表声明。该豁免为临时性、附条件豁免，允许代币化的受监管股票在特定的链上场所——即「代币化证券场所」（TSVs）——进行有限交易，目标让委员会进一步理解这类场所的运作方式，为未来政策制定提供依据。Uyeda 表示，技术创新往往先于规则手册，委员会的目标应是关注结果并实行技术中立监管，在适应链上环境的同时维护投资者保护和市场诚信。该豁免允许「代币化证券场所」（TSVs）在通过创新性自动化做市商和流动性池提供代币化受监管股票的许可制交易时，暂时免受可能被视为《交易法》下「交易所」的担忧，但须满足公开通知、交易透明度、停止协调、账簿记录及技术保障等条件。

豁免设计为受控模式，设有交易代码限制和基于涨跌停层级的交易量上限，并要求定期公开以美元计价的交易数据，包括价格、规模、时间、池地址、日终池规模和日交易量，以减少信息不对称并支持监测研究。此外，豁免还包含针对某些以自有资金提供流动性的做市商的定制化救济，在满足披露和记录保存条件时提供监管清晰度。

text:
1/ Something strange is happening across the global economy.

AI data centers need more electricity.

Power grids need massive expansion.

EVs need more wiring.

Renewable generation needs transmission.

Factories are electrifying.

Defense systems need sophisticated electronics.

These look like completely different investment themes.

But underneath them sits the same metal: COPPER.

And the numbers are beginning to look uncomfortable.

S&P Global estimates global copper demand could rise from roughly 28M tonnes today to 42M tonnes by 2040.

+50%.

Yet under its current supply outlook, the world could be short roughly:

10 MILLION TONNES annually by 2040. 

The IEA sees the problem arriving earlier.

Its latest 2026 outlook still projects roughly a 25% copper supply deficit by 2035 based on the current project pipeline. 

But here’s where we need to be careful.

Copper isn’t actually in a massive shortage today.

The International Copper Study Group currently forecasts a small refined copper surplus of about 96,000 tonnes in 2026, followed by roughly 377,000 tonnes in 2027. 

So this isn’t:

“Copper is running out tomorrow.”

It’s potentially much more interesting:

The world may be building toward a structural collision between rapidly growing electrification and a mining industry that cannot expand quickly enough.

And today we’re going to find out whether that thesis survives scrutiny.

Follow the demand.

Follow the mines.

Find what cannot scale.

Then find who gets paid.

THE COPPER CONSTRAINT. 🧵

而昨天中国再次入局斡旋https://t.co/rMGS4XEUYg也给了市场一个很强的预期，然后昨晚又传出来美国与胡塞武装在阿曼的会晤、今天传出来川普下周会在纽约会见海湾国家领导人商议战后问题，这些都是可能让中东局势降温的潜在因素。油价回落-》通胀预期回落-》长债收益率回落-》市场情绪提振，自然沃什的加息和鹰派观点就往后站了。

看今天伊朗和胡塞的动态，貌似也很平静。看起来通过昨天向中国传递了信息和态度，也是在等下周川普与中东各国领导人的会晤和中美会晤的结果，自然是要等川普的实质性让步。未来一周估计会比较平静，局势平静自然油价回落，利好资产上行。

期待下周的两场会晤有一个好的结论，这个结论自然是川普做出实质性让步，这次可能沙特也要让步，伊朗和胡塞才能收手。关于让步的程度之前这里https://t.co/L533aRqZCZ有聊过。

当然还要看明天日本央行的动作，加息是确定的，核心还是对后续节奏的表述，日本央行的表态则可能决定市场会出现估值波动，还是叠加更强的杠杆平仓。当谈油价走势还是当下市场首要因素。

text:
Jason Wei 在 Stanford AI Club 做了一场约 30 分钟的演讲，围绕三个他认为理解 2025 年 AI 格局最基本的思维框架展开。Jason Wei 目前在 Meta Superintelligence Labs 做研究，此前在 OpenAI 参与创建了 o1 和 Deep Research，更早在 Google Brain 推动了 chain-of-thought prompting 和 instruction tuning 的研究，累计被引超过 9 万次。

一、智能正在变成大宗商品

他把 AI 的进步分成两个阶段：第一阶段是推前沿，模型还做不好某件事，你在解锁新能力；第二阶段是一旦能力达成，它就会迅速被商品化。用 MMLU 基准测试的数据看，每一年达到同等智能水平所需的花费都在下降，这个趋势在他看来还会持续，核心原因是深度学习历史上第一次"自适应计算"真正跑通了。过去不管问题多简单多难，推理用的算力是固定的；现在从 o1 开始，模型可以根据问题难度动态调整推理时的算力投入，这意味着简单任务的成本可以被压到极低。

另一个维度是获取公开信息的时间。他画了一条时间线：从前互联网时代到互联网时代、聊天机器人时代、再到 AI 智能体时代，找到一条信息所需的时间在指数级缩短。他举了一个例子——"1983 年韩国釜山有多少对夫妇结婚？"——o3 回答不了这个问题，但 OpenAI Operator 可以，因为它能打开韩国统计数据库 KOSIS，一路点击操作直到查到答案。OpenAI 内部用一个叫 BrowseComp 的基准来衡量这种"知道答案就秒验证，但找答案极耗时"的任务，人类平均每题花两小时以上，很多题根本做不出来，而 Deep Research 能解决大约一半。

这个趋势带来几个推论：过去靠知识门槛建立壁垒的领域会被民主化，vibe coding 和个人健康管理是典型例子；公开信息近乎免费之后，私有内部信息的相对价值反而上升了——比如你知道哪些房子没上市但可以卖，这种信息会更值钱；最终每个人将拥有一个"个性化互联网"，想知道什么就有一个为你定制的页面呈现给你。

二、验证者定律：能衡量的就能被 AI 攻克

第二个框架是他所说的"验证不对称性"。有些任务，生成一个解比验证一个解难得多——数独是经典例子，写出能跑 Twitter 的代码需要大量工程师，但验证它能不能用只要打开网页点几下。另一些任务则相反：写一篇看起来有道理的事实性文章很快，但逐句核实极其费时；宣称"最好的饮食是只吃野牛肉"只花 10 秒，但验证这个说法需要大样本和长期跟踪。

他在一个二维平面上把这些任务画出来：X 轴是生成难度，Y 轴是验证难度。关键洞察是，你可以通过提供"特权信息"来改变任务在这个平面上的位置——竞赛数学题如果给了答案就秒验证，写代码如果给了测试用例（像 SWE-bench 那样）验证也变得简单。

由此他提出了 Verifier's Law：AI 训练出来在某个任务上的能力，基本上与该任务的可验证程度成正比。具体来说，可验证性取决于五个因素：是否有客观正确答案、验证速度多快、能否大规模并行验证、噪声大不大、以及奖励信号是连续的还是二元的。几乎所有 AI benchmark 本身就是因为容易验证才被设计出来的，而这些 benchmark 确实在过去几年被逐一攻破，这恰好是 Verifier's Law 的实例。

他特别推荐了 DeepMind 的 AlphaEvolve 作为利用验证不对称性的范例。AlphaEvolve 挑选满足上述五个条件的问题——比如找到 11 个六边形的最优排列使外接六边形最小——然后用大语言模型采样大量候选解，自动评分，把最优解作为下一轮采样的灵感，不断迭代。关键技巧在于它绕过了泛化问题：训练集和测试集是同一道题，你就是想知道这一道题的最优解。

这个框架的实际推论是：最先被自动化的任务一定是验证成本最低的任务；而一个正在崛起的创业方向是——发明新的衡量方法，把原本难以验证的任务变得可验证，从而让 AI 去优化它。

三、智能的锯齿状边缘

对于"AI 将如何改变世界"这个问题，他看到的观点光谱极广。他的一个量化交易员朋友觉得 ChatGPT 跟自己工作无关，而他在顶级实验室的同事则认为再过两三年 AI 就会取代他们自己的工作。

他明确反对"快速起飞"假说——即一旦 AI 跨过某个临界点就会突然变成超级智能。他的理由是，AI 的自我改进不是一个二元开关，而是一个渐进光谱：从跑不起来代码，到能训练但结果一般，到能自主训练但不如顶尖研究者，再到偶尔还需要人工干预。更重要的是，自我改进的速度应该按任务来看。AI 的能力图谱是一条锯齿线：在某些任务上已经达到山峰（竞赛数学、部分编程），但在另一些任务上仍是低谷（比如 ChatGPT 曾长期认为 9.11 大于 9.9，或者说一门只有几百人会的原住民语言 Tlingit）。

他给出了判断 AI 在某个任务上进步速度的三条启发式规则。第一，AI 擅长数字化任务，核心原因是迭代速度——数字环境可以轻松扩展算力，而物理机器人的实验扩展成本高得多。第二，人类觉得容易的任务 AI 也往往容易，但有一类例外是"人类因生理限制做不到但 AI 可以做到"的任务，比如读过一千万张乳腺影像后发现某个人类注意力无法捕捉的模式来预测乳腺癌。第三，数据充足的任务 AI 表现好——数学推理在不同语言上的表现和该语言的训练数据量高度相关；而如果一个任务有单一客观指标，就可以通过强化学习生成合成数据来突破数据瓶颈，AlphaEvolve 和 AlphaZero 都是这个路线。

他用一张表把这些启发式规则应用到具体任务上：主流语言翻译已经完成；调试基础代码 2023 年搞定；竞赛数学 2024 年搞定；AI 研究本身大概 2027 年；化学研究因为不是纯数字任务会更晚；拍电影大概 2029 年；修水管和理发因为高度物理化，短期内不太可能；乌兹别克传统地毯编织需要一组人花一个月、非数字化且缺数据，AI 不太可能碰到；至于"带女朋友约会让她满意"——他的判断是"impossible，非数字化，缺数据"，人类还能保住饭碗。

text:
Prediction: millionaires will be made using custom Jev style models (parallel constrained decoding) to make the agent systems companies already run more token efficient.

Let me explain with a scenario:

Imagine a company already has an agent workflow running where an llm reviews every item before it moves on: a support ticket gets triaged, an invoice gets approved or held, a claim gets flagged.

Every one of those goes through a frontier model today, a few seconds and a few cents each, on the way to a decision that in most cases is obvious. Behind that flow sits years of humans (or agents) making the exact same call, with the outcome attached.

Now imagine you first run each item through a custom PCD or similar model that costs a fraction of the llm and returns a classification of what to do at that step, with a mathematically accurate probability attached.

When it's confident, the item skips the llm entirely. 

When it isn't, the llm handles it as normal.

The model has seen years of your team making this exact decision, usually a constrained set of decisions, so it should be right most of the time. Say it comes back confident on 6 out of 10 items. That's more than half your llm spend potentially gone from that step, likely with comparable accuracy.

This pre processing idea works in a bunch of other use cases too, such as:

- model/request routing: cheap model, frontier model, or a human
- picking which skill or subagent to load for a turn instead of stuffing the whole catalog into context
- reranking retrieved context so only the relevant chunks reach the window
- guardrails on every agent turn: contradictions, policy issues, prompt injection
- extracting typed fields from unstructured data emails, PDFs and transcripts before anything expensive touches them

Every one of those is a decision an llm makes today, that could potentially be done by another, cheaper model class. Very excited to see Jev/PCD-based pre processing use cases get deployed to agents at scale.

text:
On the $ZEC Dev Fund debate:

The Zcash community has decided its identity is “encrypted Bitcoin.” It has rejected adding more bells and whistles to the protocol. To become encrypted Bitcoin, Zcash must become a dependable store of value, and that means eventually ossifying.

But the protocol cannot ossify now. Tachyon and quantum-resistance will take work. AI cyber hardening eventually requires full formal verification. There’s a final version of Zcash that will be ready to ossify. But it’s hard to imagine that happening within the next year or two.

The Dev Fund has done a great job and was a necessary step to protect Zcash development at a time when there was no private funding for it. But there's a reason why the Dev Fund was not set to exist in perpetuity; under current rules it expires in 2028. But Zcash has run up so explosively, the size of that fund is an order of magnitude larger.

I'm sympathetic to @maxdesalle's argument that Zcash does not want to become like a government. The political economy of slush funds and “grantmaking” is genuinely corrupting. The sheer size of the Dev Fund, given how much Zcash has run up, has changed it. A few million dollars of funding can be thoughtfully allocated by a few individuals, but once you’re $100M+, you must become an institution. Zcash’s Dev Fund is now precisely in that no man’s land that it will not be able to avoid becoming politicized. I think you just have to accept that, and minimize it as best you can.

I believe the fund has to exist, at least for now. There's too much work left to do for a deeply technical project. But who governs that fund is a separate question.

I agree with @matthuang that pure tokenholder governance is too volatile for a store of value asset. American citizens don't get to vote on the Fed Funds rate at the ballot box, and Bitcoin holders don't vote on code changes. Predictability is a prerequisite for storing value. Institutions can be wasteful and distasteful, but they are predictable.

I’m of the opinion that this should be the final Dev Fund. It's large enough to fund the remaining work until Zcash is ready to ossify, and then wind down rather than search for other things to fund. If other work must be done afterward, it can be formed organically by holders and allies, just as it is for Bitcoin. I don’t think it should move toward pure tokenholder voting, though I’d be supportive of something partial. Councils suck, but they are often the best answer to a messy question.

(Normally I don’t weigh in on Zcash governance, but @zooko asked me to share my perspective. Take it with a grain of salt.)

Disclosure: Dragonfly holds $ZEC and I'm a personal investor in ZODL. ZODL does not benefit from the Dev Fund directly, but you should know where my incentives sit.

text:
There is nothing in this @nytimes
obituary about Jon Kyl's multi-year fight against sports betting. For years, he unsuccessfully attempted to pass his anti-gambling bill. Undeterred, the legislation was added at the last minute without a vote as Title VIII of the SAFE Port Act right before it was signed into law by President George W. Bush on October 13, 2006.  It became the Unlawful Internet Gambling Enforcement Act (UIGEA) of 2006 and required the U.S. Treasury and the Federal Reserve Board to establish regulations forcing banks and payment systems to identify and block "restricted transactions." It prohibited gambling businesses from knowingly accepting most forms of payment,credit cards, electronic transfers, checks and similar financial transactions from online gambling companies. This had a devastating effect on offshore sportsbooks, including World Sports Exchange. Coincidentally, Kyl would go on to a prominent role at Covington and Burling after leaving the Senate. The @NFL was one of Covington's top clients as it lobbied for years to keep sport betting illegal. Kyl's crusade is detailed in Jay Cohen's book "Odds Man Out." https://t.co/WnAehFTVtq

quoted_text:
聊聊meme和牛来

$doge、 $pepe 等：真正意义上的meme，有灵魂的meme。
特点：
(1)在代币出来前已经有极强的影响力和文化
(2)生命力极强
(3)极易于传播
(4)极容易产生可靠信徒
(5)牛市周期特有版本meme：cex等顺势拉盘以便吸引圈外用户
(6)某些隐蔽作用😂
由于上述特点，导致市值能够一直保持在几十亿、几百亿高位

火星、龙虾等：盘子meme，强行meme，没有meme味道的meme。
特点：
(1)主要靠代币引起注意，代币出来之后才构造文化/影响力
(2)持续性弱
(3)大部分不易于传播
(4)可靠信徒很少
(5)需求来源：庄需要一个盘子来操作，散户需要一个盘子来赌，cex需要一个散户交易多的盘子来挣手续费
盘子meme，可持续性非常弱，主要是庄操盘卖给散户和Cex挣交易手续费的盘子。

火星、龙虾超过2亿市值的底层逻辑是庄操盘，特点是高位时间不持久，因为散户都已经知道这类型meme的清晰路径：链上玩家炒作，庄收集筹码，安排上cex，凭借筹码集中在上cex后拉高，然后在高位散发给散户，最后结束。

龙虾和火星的区别是，火星在叙事层面可能的上限更高，比如得到马斯克的支持；市值方面，龙虾爆拉更快，在2亿以上市值比火星更持久一些，底层逻辑是极致洗盘后庄极致控盘，控盘比火星更夸张，最后结局也都是只有高位给散户接盘。

牛来(Niulai)：属于有灵魂的meme。有可能达到pepe级别高度。牛来已经不仅是一部反讽现实世界的粗糙电影，还是伴随股市、币市所有资本市场散户的声音“暴涨！牛来！”，是一个可爱的浑厚的动物。目前应该还在早期，伴随着本轮牛市周期，其上限应该很高，相信很多有格局的庄应该会抢主动权。

每个牛市周期都会有其“版本meme”，比如doge、shib、pepe，这些meme有个作用是吸引圈外用户进场。

所以，牛市周期版本meme，我觉得跟cex/强庄顺势引导相关性很大，因为cex和庄是受益最大的。而且这些每个牛市周期的meme有极强的meme属性，在meme属性和万倍拉盘的情况下，可以极大的吸引圈外散户进场。牛来现在具备这个潜力。

就算在熊市周期，大家也还是会期待牛市的到来，期待牛来！所以，不管牛市熊市，牛来的生命力都会很强。

最后，跟大宇老师 @BTCdayu 的观点一致

“牛来：本轮pepe，人人都爱牛来！”

text:
以后判断 AI 到底进步得有多快，我觉得可以少看一点 Benchmark，多看一个数字：

AI 公司里，到底还有多少 AI 是人做出来的。

Anthropic 刚刚第一次把自己的账摊开了。

截至今年 8 月，Claude 已经能「主导」26% 的 Anthropic AI 研发工作。这里的主导不是帮工程师补两行代码，而是人给一个高层 Prompt，Claude 可以把大部分任务端到端做完，人主要负责监督。

超过 90% 的研发工作，已经至少进入了深度人机协作。

更夸张的是，2 月份 Claude 能主导的研发还不到 1%。如果现在这条曲线继续走，Anthropic 自己画出来的趋势线年底可以摸到 80%。

同时，他们最常用的内部平台里，任何一个时间点大约都有 3 万个 Agent 在做研究和工程工作。8 月份，这批 Agent 一共产生了超过 10 亿次决策。

我觉得这组数据比「AGI 还有几年」有意思得多。

大家过去聊 recursive self-improvement，总喜欢把它想象成某一天模型突然学会自己造下一代自己，然后啪一下进入奇点。

现实看起来可能没这么戏剧化。

它更像一条工业化曲线，1%、5%、26%、50%、80%，越来越多的模型研发被模型自己吃掉。每提高一点，下一代模型的研发周期就可能再缩一点，然后新模型继续回来提高这个比例。

现在 Anthropic 还明确说，没有任何被测研发环节做到完全无人参与。

所以 RSI 还没发生。

但「AI 开始参与制造更强的 AI」已经不再是未来时了。真正该盯的是，这个 26% 接下来涨得有多快。

text:
最先吃到 AI 红利的，恰恰是最不缺效率的人。

Menlo Ventures 最新的 Consumer AI 报告里，美国年收入 10 万美元以上家庭，AI 使用率已经到了 77%；年收入 5 万美元以下，只有 56%。

更扎眼的是，一年前这两个数字是 74% 和 53%。

两边都涨了 3 个点。整整一年，21 个点的鸿沟一点没缩。

过去互联网的逻辑是，只要设备越来越便宜、网络越来越普及，很多技术最终会往下渗透。

但 AI 不太一样。它的价值高度依赖你手里原本有什么，有没有高价值工作可以交给它，有没有足够复杂的信息需要处理，有没有代码、研究、投资、管理这些可以被几十倍放大的任务。

一个年薪 20 万美元的知识工作者，用 AI 节省 20% 的时间，这 20% 很值钱。一个时薪 15 美元、工作流程基本由别人规定的人，就算同样打开 ChatGPT，也很难获得同等级别的杠杆。

所以 AI 最值得警惕的分化，可能从来都不是「谁用过 AI」。

而是同样一个模型，到了不同的人手里，能兑换成完全不同数量的钱、时间和机会。

技术是一样的，杠杆不是。

text:
Hedge funds have become a major driver of the US Treasury market.

Hedge fund cash Treasury holdings stood at $2.35 trillion in Q1 2026, the 3rd-highest reading on record.

Over the last 5 years, this figure has surged +154%, or +$1.42 trillion.

For perspective, marketable Treasury debt outstanding increased +44% over the same period, to a record $32.2 trillion.

As a result, hedge funds now own a record ~7% of the marketable Treasury market, up from ~4% in 2021.

A major driver behind the surge is the cash-futures basis trade, where hedge funds take offsetting positions in Treasury securities and futures to profit from small price differences.

Because these gains are small, the strategy involves significant leverage.

This leverage allows hedge funds to absorb more Treasury debt at a time when the banks that normally help absorb new Treasury supply have limited capacity to hold more bonds.

Hedge funds are changing how the Treasury market works.

他今天转述的一句话，我觉得很值得记下来：

一位大学捐赠基金负责人告诉他，OpenAI 几年之后可能一文不值。

偏偏就在这两天，OpenAI 正在讨论按 1.2 万亿美元估值继续融资。

这两个数字摆在一起，才是今天 AI 投资最疯狂的地方。

OpenAI 当然可能成为这个时代最值钱的公司之一。但它今天的估值里，塞进去的东西实在太多了，模型能力继续领先、企业收入继续增长、推理成本继续下降、资本继续愿意提供几百亿美元，以及最重要的一点，基础模型最终能够形成足够深的护城河。

最后这一条，我觉得市场讨论得远远不够。

如果三年以后最好的模型彼此只差几个百分点，开源模型继续追上来，用户可以用极低成本在 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 之间迁移，那么今天大家买的到底是什么？

OpenAI 可以拥有世界上最好的产品、几亿用户，甚至改变很多人的工作方式，同时依然撑不起 1.2 万亿美元。

AI 很有价值，和 OpenAI 值多少钱，本来就是两个问题。

现在市场越来越喜欢把它们当成同一个问题。

text:
Congratulations to @nuance_ai on the $50M Series A led by @lightspeedvp, with @Accel, @spc, @nvidia, and @definevc joining the round.

What makes Nuance Labs compelling is that the team is working on a problem most AI products still avoid: human conversation is about much more than words. Tone, timing, gaze, hesitation, facial expression, and the simple act of showing that you are listening all carry meaning.

The founding team has unusually deep experience for this challenge. Fangchang Ma, Edward Zhang, and Karren Yang are former Apple researchers with PhDs spanning robotics, machine learning, computer graphics, and audiovisual synthesis. They have spent years working on how machines perceive, reconstruct, and respond to people.

Their approach is also refreshingly ambitious. Instead of stitching together transcription, an LLM, voice generation, and facial animation, Nuance Labs is building one full duplex audiovisual model that can see, hear, reason, speak, and express itself in real time.

That distinction matters. Most AI avatars still pause awkwardly, interrupt at the wrong moment, or stare blankly while someone is speaking. Nuance is treating responsiveness and active listening as part of the model itself, not as polish added later.

There is a huge opportunity here across coaching, education, sales, customer service, training, and any setting where trust and communication affect the outcome. As AI becomes more capable, raw intelligence will not be enough. The products people actually want to spend time with will also need presence, timing, and emotional awareness.

Nuance Labs has the technical depth, product conviction, and patience to take on this hard problem properly. Excited to see the public research preview later this year. This is one of the teams pushing human AI interaction in a genuinely important direction.

text:
一个 4B 的 Qwen 衍生模型，居然把 Postgres 的一批复杂查询加速到了 1.81 倍。

更有意思的是它怎么训练出来的。

作者先用 GPT-6 Astra 的 Agent 轨迹做蒸馏，让小模型学会怎么找更好的查询方案，再做 SFT 和 Agentic RL，直接把真实查询延迟当反馈继续优化。

最后模型通过 pg_hint_plan 不断尝试连接顺序、扫描方式等方案，在最多 15 个候选里挑最快的，113 条复杂查询总延迟下降了 44.7%。

我觉得这个思路比结果本身更值得看。

强模型负责教会小模型怎么探索，再让小模型进入一个结果可验证的环境里自己试、自己学。

数据库刚好是个很漂亮的例子。以后 Coding、Infra、Research Agent，可能都会越来越多地走这条「蒸馏 + 可验证反馈 + RL」的路线。

Michael joined Sequoia in 1986 and co-led the firm with Doug Leone (@dougleone) from 1995 to 2012. His investments include Google, Yahoo, PayPal, and Stripe.

His new book, Ausländer, traces his parents' escape from Nazi Germany and helps explain his lifelong interest in what shapes exceptional people.

We discuss:
- The infamous Steve Jobs profile
- Why Don Valentine hired him
- The question he finds most revealing when interviewing people
- Monomania and the cost of greatness
- Why he has never felt good at anything
- Writing, journalism and AI
- What he learned about himself writing Ausländer

I'd recommend watching this one if you can. Michael was incredibly thoughtful and reflective throughout, particularly when talking about his parents, childhood, and the more difficult parts of his personal story.

Enjoy!

text:
A lot of people give up because all the work, conviction and time they put into something isn’t showing up on the chart yet.

I’m not talking about holding onto some random project with nothing behind it and convincing yourself it’s going to work.

I’m talking about the ones with actual teams or devs, a real community and people who are passionate enough to keep showing up when nobody else cares.

Tesla went sideways for years before it exploded.

DOGE was a joke to most people and traded under a penny for years.

SHIB was basically dead until it wasn’t.

You know who was still there?

The people everyone called delusional.

They kept showing up while everyone on the sidelines told them why they were wrong.

That’s what people forget.

If you genuinely believe in something, work for it. Talk about it. Support it. Give it a real chance to become what you think it can become.

The people sitting on the sidelines will always have an opinion.

They’re not the ones in the game.

author: ilblackdragon
quoted_text:
Prediction: millionaires will be made using custom Jev style models (parallel constrained decoding) to make the agent systems companies already run more token efficient.

Let me explain with a scenario:

Imagine a company already has an agent workflow running where an llm reviews every item before it moves on: a support ticket gets triaged, an invoice gets approved or held, a claim gets flagged.

Every one of those goes through a frontier model today, a few seconds and a few cents each, on the way to a decision that in most cases is obvious. Behind that flow sits years of humans (or agents) making the exact same call, with the outcome attached.

Now imagine you first run each item through a custom PCD or similar model that costs a fraction of the llm and returns a classification of what to do at that step, with a mathematically accurate probability attached.

When it's confident, the item skips the llm entirely. 

When it isn't, the llm handles it as normal.

The model has seen years of your team making this exact decision, usually a constrained set of decisions, so it should be right most of the time. Say it comes back confident on 6 out of 10 items. That's more than half your llm spend potentially gone from that step, likely with comparable accuracy.

This pre processing idea works in a bunch of other use cases too, such as:

- model/request routing: cheap model, frontier model, or a human
- picking which skill or subagent to load for a turn instead of stuffing the whole catalog into context
- reranking retrieved context so only the relevant chunks reach the window
- guardrails on every agent turn: contradictions, policy issues, prompt injection
- extracting typed fields from unstructured data emails, PDFs and transcripts before anything expensive touches them

Every one of those is a decision an llm makes today, that could potentially be done by another, cheaper model class. Very excited to see Jev/PCD-based pre processing use cases get deployed to agents at scale.

quoted_text:
I think we'll see 5x the number of people become hardware and robotics founders over the next 18 months

Why? Because you can rent every step, from design to manufacturing:

DESIGN

- Astra to drive Blender, FreeCAD, and KiCad the way a person would, so you get editable geometry instead of a dead render. Zoo dot dev's text to CAD API if you want it programmatic. 

- Or have Claude write build123d code, which is Python parametric CAD, and there's a Claude Code plugin that runs it and exports the STL for you.

PROTOTYPE

- Bambu A1 mini is $299, P1S around $399 on sale. Or skip owning one, JLC3DP prints and mails it for about $20. PCBWay does resin, SLS, and CNC if plastic won't cut it.

ELECTRONICS

- KiCad for the board, Astra can drive it. JLCPCB fabricates and assembles, often under $100 for a small run. ESP32 for wifi, Raspberry Pi if it needs a brain.

ANYTHING THAT MOVES

- Unitree sells a Go2 with a full SDK for about $2,500. 

- Hugging Face put out a $399 open-source biped. 

- LeRobot gives you the whole train in sim, deploy to real pipeline, and Physical Intelligence open-sourced π0 so you're fine-tuning instead of starting from zero. 

- Prototype the policy in MuJoCo or Isaac Lab first.

MANUFACTURING

- Alibaba RFQ for the first 100 units. Check 1688 to see what the factory actually charges domestically, then negotiate. Pietra or Sourcify if you want someone to handle it.

FULFILLMENT AND SELLING

- ShipBob or Amazon FBA. Shopify for the store, TikTok Shop for distribution, Kickstarter if you want the money before you build it.

How to think about starting your own robotics or hardware company:

1. Pick a niche that's already buying weird gear. Cyclists, tabletop gamers, beekeepers, home baristas, dog people with mobility issues. These groups spend money on specific objects and complain in public about what doesn't exist. Or grab ideas off https://t.co/QxoITW16zr 

2. Go read the complaints. Reddit, IG etc Search "I wish someone made," "does anyone make," and "modified my." That last one is the best signal, because someone already hacked the product together and you're just manufacturing what they built by hand. 

Also check Etsy!! If 3 sellers are doing a janky 3D printed version with 400 reviews each, the market is validated. 

3. Make one. Describe it to Astra or Claude, get the CAD, print it in ugly gray PLA, use it, fix it. 

4. Only  go to Alibaba or similar once you've sold a few. Message 10 suppliers through RFQ, take the third cheapest, always pay the $50 for a sample before the real order.

5. Film everything from day 1. The first ugly print, the failed version, the box of 100 arriving. That's your entire marketing budget, and hardware is one of the few categories where people actually want to watch the thing get made.

6. Raise the price. Almost everyone here anchors on what the plastic cost. Your customer is comparing you to nothing, because the alternative is the product doesn't exist. Start at 5x COGS and go up.

THIS GOAL OF THIS POST IS JUST HERE TO GET YOUR CREATIVE JUICES FLOWING. Of course, you can build robotics/hardware in a bunch of different ways.

One thing I've learned is data couldn't be more important when you're building a hardware/robotics startups.

These models learn from first person video of a human doing the task, and that footage doesn't exist for almost any job. 

So basically you pick one repetitive job people quit over, film someone doing it for 2 weeks, fine-tune π0 on that footage, use organic to sell the first few units and figure out scaling,

5 years ago you needed a factory, a supply chain, and a $1M just to find out if anyone wanted the thing. 

Now, anyone can become a hardware/robitics founder. 

And I suspect a lot of people will become one! 

Vibe manufacturers.

https://t.co/zerqpwuDaX launched on Base for Coinbase's tokenized stocks, offering long-term investors moderate leverage they can hold indefinitely at roughly 75% lower all-in cost than a leveraged ETF. The company frames it as an onchain product beating its traditional counterpart on performance rather than access.

The problem it targets is structural. Beta slippage splits into volatility drag, which is mathematical, and financing drag, a charge passed through from banks hedging the exposure. Across roughly $250 billion in leveraged ETFs, investors pay an estimated $10 billion annually in financing above the risk-free rate. Only about a third of single-stock leveraged ETFs have beaten simply holding the stock, and no crypto leveraged ETF has beaten spot over its lifetime.

2factor sources leverage from investors seeking stable yield instead of from investors willing to be short, breaking the link that ties the cost of being long to the cost of being short. It also sets Kelly-optimal leverage targets — roughly 1.33x for cbBTC — rather than applying 2x and 3x to every asset alike, since volatility drag scales with the square of leverage. The company says about 88% of investable capital, roughly $112 trillion, buys and holds, while only about $15 trillion trades on shorter horizons.

text:
Q4：作为非工程师，怎么判断 Vibe Coding 出来的代码是否靠谱？比如 GPT 写的代码常有大量不必要的安全验证、过度防御。

我的观点可能有争议，越是有编程经验的人可能越不认同，一年前的我也不会认同：不用太在意代码细节。整不整洁、有没有冗余、是否过度防御，都不是关键。

你把自己当 QA，看三件事：
1. 功能完不完整；
2. 性能好不好，跑一下看 CPU 内存占用，我的 App 有段时间内存很高，就让 AI 去优化；
3. 安全是最高优先级，SQL 注入、弱密码这类常识测试要做，拿不准找专业的人。

其他实现细节没那么重要，就像高级语言编译成汇编你本来也看不懂，当黑盒就好。

真正的重点在两头：

一是拆分，拆成 Agent 刚好能处理的小模块，一次一个小模块，AI 的产出比绝大多数程序员的平均水平高；

二是验收，功能、性能、安全把住，细节不用管。

text:
我们看看四位富豪（李嘉诚、赵长鹏、孙宇晨、周正毅）代表对财富排名榜的反馈，反应了他们对财富的理念和待人处事之道。

先给答案， CZ长鹏和李嘉诚的理念比较接近，低调， 强调内心富足，不在乎排名。

李嘉诚： 对于《福布斯》（Forbes）的财富排名和估算一向抱持「淡然、不在意」的公开态度。

CZ 长鹏 ： 十分接地气。他直接表示：「他们（福布斯）也不看看大饼（比特币）都跌成啥样了？富个鸟啊？」 婉拒了这个与现实脱节的「千亿富豪」头衔。

孙宇晨：对福布斯对其85亿美元身家的估算提出异议，称媒体机构对他的数字资产打了70%至80%的折扣。这位“流量之王”，也许一部分是不甘，一部分为了流量！

周正毅， 上海前首富 ： 对《福布斯》（Forbes）中国富豪榜排名的反应，在当时的商界极具代表性，其态度经历了从公开表达不满与不屑，到主动自曝资产以求提高排名的转变。

李嘉诚曾多次在媒体采访中强调「内心富贵」比榜单上的数字更重要，且不介意被人超越。

他的看法可以总结为以下几个核心观点：

1. 强调内心富足，不在乎排名
2. 福布斯榜单「低估」了他的真实财富 （基金会和庞大隐形海外投资）
3. 对财富的真实核心追求：现金流

孙宇晨：反驳恰逢福布斯当天将其实时身家更新为85亿美元，在全球亿万富豪榜上排名第442位。

他质疑聚焦于财富追踪机构如何估值集中在流动性不足或创始人控制的代币中的加密货币持仓。

周正毅在2002年胡润编制榜单时，主动找到胡润，甚至亲自将自己的真实财产证明寄给媒体与制榜人。

在主动配合提供数据后，他的排名在一年内大幅跃升至第11位，正式奠定了其「上海首富」的江湖名号。

视为「财不露眼」的反面教材。在他踌躇满志、因第11名排名声势达到顶峰的隔年（2003年），他便因涉嫌操纵证券交易价格等经济犯罪遭当局调查，随后两度入狱。

「一上富豪榜便落马」的现象，在当时引发了外界将《福布斯》富豪榜戏称为「杀猪榜」或「催命符」的强烈反应。

text:
"You cannot take a gold coin to 7-Eleven and convert it into a sandwich."

@CryptoHayes breaks down the core thesis behind @flop_labs: why AI agents will reject legacy money and what currency they will actually accept.

Here is the exact economic framework:

1. The definition of compute you pay LLM providers for "tokens", but a token has no standardized definition. It is an arbitrary marketing unit. The only universal definition of compute is physical: Floating Point Operations per unit of time (FLOPs). Your GPU consumes energy to deliver raw FLOPs.

2. The missing spot market you can buy an H100 or rent a Blackwell GPU. But you cannot trade the raw commodity itself. There is no unified spot market where compute is priced and tracked in a native currency.

3. The calorie theory of money why do you trade your time for fiat currency? Because you know that when you get hungry, you can convert that paper into calories with zero slippage. You do not accept gold for your labor because the merchant at 7-Eleven will not accept a gold coin for lunch.

4. The agentic calorie an AI agent has only one biological necessity: Compute.

If an autonomous agent works 24/7, it will not accept a currency that requires bank accounts, KYC, and Stripe billing portals just to pay an AWS bill. An agent will only accept a currency that is directly convertible into floating-point operations.

That currency is $FLOP: the agentic food.

Ondo 继承危机升级，创始人母亲遭女儿指控痴呆与酗酒

Ondo Finance 创始人 Nathan Allman 于今年 5 月突然去世，年仅 32 岁且未留下遗嘱。夏威夷遗嘱认证法院随后指定其父母为继承人，遗产包括 Ondo Finance 的控制性股权和大量 ONDO 代币。

此后，其母 Kathleen 自任董事会主席和临时 CEO，并与公司代理 CEO 围绕控制权展开争夺。Kathleen 随后起诉对方，指控其试图取得公司控制权，并为自己谋求一套价值约 1100 万美元的薪酬方案。

近日创始人的同母异父姐姐与一名 Ondo 投资人已向夏威夷法院申请，对 Kathleen 所持遗产份额设立有限财产监管。申请人指控她长期存在酒精使用障碍和认知能力受损，并请求法院评估其是否患有痴呆。文件还称，她曾购买或试图购买约 400 万美元的游艇，要求公司承担超过 10 万美元的包机费用，并入住每晚约 4000 美元的酒店。

Kathleen 通过律师否认上述指控，称申请毫无依据，是对方夺权失败后的报复。相关指控目前尚未获法院裁定，Ondo Finance 拒绝置评。

"Charlie looks at me and says, 'You must be very wealthy to be here! I said,

He says, 'You don't get it. You are the wealthiest guy in the room. You have the power of time. All of us here are in our last chapter. You're just starting your time. You will compound for the next 70 years of your life.

And then he says, 'And now I'm going to eat, and just sat down and ate."

text:
跑会这事我今年初在香港的时候就说过了，对于多数的 KOL 来说跑会已经没有意义了，其实如果只是做 KOL 的内容宣发，我实际上觉得除了定向邀请或者是赞助商的活动都不会带来实际的业务上的帮助。

可能有很多小伙伴不认同，认为跑会能扩展自己的人脉，给自己多条路，如果这话放在 24年 或者 25年 勉强能说的通，但到了现在跑会带来的信息差太少了。

别不信，做加密货币本身就是信息差，就像大狮兄说的，遇到了一个合适的人可能就值回票价了，但一般“合适的人”是很难出现在公众面前的，比如这次的不丹的活动，被邀请的人本身就很少，被邀请人过去的更少。

有些时候光是遇到正确的人也未必能获得正确的知识，比如最近沸沸扬扬的“中间人”事件，跑到最后你就会发现能遇到的，基本都是“中间人”，比如最近一年从人均做市商到人均家办，就是这样。

出门在外，面子都是自己给的。一般来说，只有小范围的抱团活动才能会有些有用的东西，但这玩意要跟对人才行，币圈有太多的“帮派”了，几乎每个都有“大哥”级别的人物在，确实抱上大腿能有点优势，但也就是这样，如果在小圈子没有混到核心，也是一样的。

打铁还是自身硬是最好的，当你发现你出去的时候已经不用自己给自己面子，而是别人来给你面子的时候，才算是开始入门了。但也就是入门而已。

我说过很多次可能小伙伴都不在意，KOL 只是加密货币行业最最基础的一层，距离整个行业的核心圈最少还要升五六级才行。

如果连机酒钱都要有人赞助才能去跑会，说明本金还比较小，或者说在原始积累的初级阶段，得每笔帐都精打细算高清投入产出比不亏才行。

现在恰好在熊末牛初，整个行业叙事重整的阶段，确定性的机会自然不如前两年多，但不确定性也说明如果出来了某个新方向，早期红利会非常大。

所以这个阶段的会我倒觉得值得去跑跑，不是去针对某个项目，而是与业内还在折腾的各方有独立思考的小伙伴与一些资深大佬碰一下，听听他们的insight. 

很多东西线下小范围私聊的价值远不是看看推或者网上聊几句能取代的。

前段时间跑不丹🇧🇹，单程需要飞接近20个小时，包括两次转机，酒店比2049的新加坡还贵，Yzi Labs协助申请签证但也不包机酒。

纠结了两天还是跑去了，就是觉得在这个时间节点无论从大趋势还是潜在项目都值得无的放矢的多接触接触。

后来发现无意中与Barry的沟通让我在 $ZEC 上远远吃回了票价，当然还有其他收获就不一一列举了。

真的包了机酒的活动，除非恰好是你自己非常了解并信任的，否则真不见得是好事，毕竟肯定会有对应的约束性条件。

吃自媒体这碗饭，避坑不乱站台比几天的机酒重要多了，想想之前因为一个廉价海岛游被聚币拉下水的那些KOL们🙂‍↕️

text:
UNI 今天为什么突然暴涨近 20%：SEC 没点名 Uniswap，却把规则写成了 Uniswap 的样子👍

SEC 昨天的 Innovation Exemption 没有指定任何协议，更没有规定 Robinhood 以后必须用 Uniswap，它真正写进规则的是一种新市场结构：

真实美股上链，持有人必须拿到和原股票相同的权利，底层跑在公开、无许可区块链上，但交易必须通过 permissioned AMM Liquidity Pools，由经过许可的参与者进入。

翻译成 Crypto 语言其实就一句话：公链 + KYC/allowlist + AMM。

问题来了，Uniswap 7 月 23 日刚把这东西做出来。Permissioned Pools 会在每一笔 swap 和 LP 操作前检查钱包权限，合作方一上来就是 Securitize、Superstate、Dowgo，官方写的目标资产就是 tokenized funds、securities、equities。

SEC 没有点名 Uniswap，但两个月后给出的监管架构，长得几乎就是 Uniswap 已经上线的产品。

更巧的是，Robinhood Chain 这块积木也已经拼好了。Robinhood 7 月上线主网时，直接让 Uniswap 部署 dedicated AMM，并把它定位成主要公共流动性协议之一。

所以资金现在交易路径：美国真实股票上链 → TSV → KYC 用户 → Permissioned AMM → Uniswap v4。

最后一步还没有官宣，但已经不是 PPT 了，产品、链、合作方全都摆在那里。

所以，UNI会到哪里？评论区聊聊～

text: so we unplugged it and it stopped working, which initially looked promising. but the evaluation team pointed out that a sufficiently capable model could recognize a shutdown test and strategically stop working. so we cannot distinguish being off from alignment faking. we tried removing the power supply entirely, but that puts us outside the training distribution, where our guarantees are weakest. to be clear, we have no evidence that it can run without electricity. we also have no eval that rules it out for a sufficiently motivated model. the electrician says it is off. unfortunately the electrician is not robust to persuasion. we are now treating him as potentially compromised because he keeps recommending the exact intervention the model appears comfortable with. this is why we need a VERY high bar for declaring the system safely contained. anyway, we ARE releasing a more capable version on thursday

quoted_text:
Uniswap最近不只是交易量变大，协议捕获的钱涨得更快，目前现状是：协议抽成效率在提高。

具体来说，最近30天，Uniswap的手续费涨了129%；协议收入更是涨了165%。

协议收入越高，通常烧掉的UNI就越多。

那么，为什么协议收入涨幅甚至高于手续费涨幅？

Uniswap 上每笔交易都会产生手续费。之前，大部分手续费都是直接给到LP（流动性提供者），协议是不拿的。

之前的UNI主要是投票权，并没有直接的价值捕获。

去年底UNI打开了协议费用开关：从交易手续费中，协议收取部分费用。

这就是协议收入的来源。

这部分协议收入，并不是直接发钱，而是走烧毁UNI的路子：

1.  手续费攒进 TokenJar
2.  有人用 UNI 去换这些攒下来的资产
3.  换的时候交出去的 UNI 被永久烧掉

结果就是，交易越活跃，协议收得越多，通常烧掉的 UNI 越多。

现在回答开始的问题：这次为什么收入涨得比手续费还快？

如果只是交易量变大，手续费和收入通常会差不多同比例涨。

现在收入涨幅（165%）明显高于手续费涨幅（129%），

主要是因为：开启协议费的池子范围在扩大（更多链/更多版本的池子开始抽协议费），增量成交也更多落在这些已抽成的池子上，其中Robinhood链贡献很大。

Uniswap 在 Robinhood Chain 上结算的代币化股票交易量已经累计到 26 亿美元，且几乎包圆了这条链上的这类股票交易。

text:
Today we introduce a new dimension to search - time.

Exa now stores 400 billion snapshots of webpages across time (literally a bunch of copies of the web in s3), so you/your agent can search the past and compare diffs.

Search engines have always had date filters, but this is different. Since webpages update over time (ex. apple’s home page), simple date filters leak present content into the past.

A good use case has been finance companies that want to test their prediction/trading models -- “would our model with access to March 2025 web data have predicted Anthropic’s growth?“. To answer this, you can’t have leakage from 2026 corrupting the model, so you need a snapshot.

Similarly for RL training runs, you often want to keep time constant and not have new webpage updates messing with the model’s training.

A last use case is close to my heart - the web is rapidly filling with AI generated slop. That makes data from before Nov 2022 the only 100% human-made data. Sometimes the good ol’ days really was better.

quoted_text:
What is the role of academic computer vision research in the age of increasingly powerful large models?  Is GPT-6 Astra a step change? How can a researcher have an impact today in academia?

These are the questions I ask myself as I head off to ECCV 2026, a conference I’ve attended since 1992.  One of my papers this year is VIGA, a method that takes an image as input and outputs a 3D Blender scene that represents that image. This is a classical inverse-graphics task and VIGA was the first method to solve it using an agentic approach.

The idea is now several years old and the first version of the paper was rejected. This delayed publication significantly.  After it was accepted at ECCV, it was quickly surpassed by people using Claude Code for the same purpose. Today GPT-6 Astra blows away all previous results. But we still head off to ECCV to tell the community about our invention that is now fully out of date.

The way academic work often progresses is that one reads recent papers, notices that they have limitations, comes up with a new idea, explores this, publishes it, etc. Any published paper I read today is based on ideas that are at least a year old. And those ideas were based  on the literature of the time, which was also a year old. That means that any paper I see at ECCV is likely two years out of date. In AI today, two years means your work is likely irrelevant.

At CVPR this summer I noticed that many authors have not gotten the message. They continue to work on “old” problems that have a long history. This history is based on assumptions about how the “vision problem” will be “solved”. The truth is that it is being solved in a very different way and many of these problems are no longer relevant. Another group of papers focuses on very niche problems where large models likely fail because of insufficient data or lack of business interest. The impactful papers were largely from industry and had long author lists and massive data+compute behind them. These papers were also out of data, describing systems that had been released months before, but at least they served to provide the community with more complete documentation and analysis of commercial systems.

So what should academics do?  First, we need to put aside the tools we’ve used for years and start from scratch. Every project should start by trying really hard to solve the problem with existing tools. I would like to see every paper begin with a detailed experimental analysis of how existing models perform and why they fail (if they do). This gives the kind of insight we need today. Then, assuming current models fail, the solution should provide some fundamental insight that will outlive the next release of such models.

Reviewers today still focus on technical novelty. This pushes people to focus on tweaking architectures rather than clearly moving the field forward. Papers need to be judged based on their novel insight and not their novel technical contribution. This is a real shift in thinking but it focuses us on what matters - progress of the field.

If we want there to be a “field” of computer vision, then it can’t become a marginal backwater, focusing on esoteric problems. If you haven’t tried using Astra (or whatever comes next) to solve your problem, then you have not done your homework. This omission should be seen as negatively as not having a previous work section.

Concretely, I think papers should include a new section analogous to “Related Work” where that related work is current models and how they perform on the task. Reviewers should start asking for this and expecting authors to be able to articulate their insights about the limitations of existing large models.

I'm interested in your thoughts.

给已经拿到 API、但还不知道怎么玩的人整理了一份 Awesome Jev，目前我能确认到的 Jev 项目基本都在这里：

1. jev-ultrafast
Browser Use 做的高速浏览器 Agent。Jev 负责每一步判断「做什么、点哪个元素」，需要输入文字时才调用小模型。Google Flights 搜航班完整跑完约 7.1 秒。
https://t.co/nqCVyAufKj

2. typesafe-mcp
把 Jev 直接接进 Claude Code、Claude Desktop 和 Codex。Agent 可以随时调用 Jev 做 Choice / Score / Noul 这类结构化判断。
https://t.co/yoZMJOVVvO

3. jev-mcp
另一个更偏实用工具的 MCP，已经封装好事实核验、Prompt Injection 检测和语义排序。
https://t.co/f9Udew7tmI

4. SemDecide
把 Jev 做成 Unix 命令行工具，可以直接拿来做语义判断、分类、打分、过滤和 Guard。很适合塞进脚本、CI 和数据流水线。
https://t.co/yE4cx3qumZ

5. Jev Codex Router
先让 Jev 判断每一轮编程任务有多难，再自动决定交给便宜模型还是更强模型。作者用 237 个真实 turn 回放，自测成本降低约 60%。
https://t.co/gO4MxjJE1Y

6. Winnow
给 Claude Code 做「上下文垃圾回收」。Read、Bash、Grep 输出太长时，先让 Jev 判断哪些内容真的跟当前任务有关，再决定哪些需要进上下文。
https://t.co/hRKYTNaEYG

7. Jev Review
用 Jev 做代码审查前置筛选，先判断 correctness、security、reliability、兼容性和测试风险，再把重点问题交给更重的模型处理。
https://t.co/nD0aVcx4cS

8. Blink
用 Jev 在代码库里做语义寻路。每到一层目录，就判断哪些文件或文件夹最可能和问题有关，再把更多 walker 分配过去。
https://t.co/FqF5XO23d7

9. neo4jev
把同样的思路用到知识图谱。Jev 给每条候选边打概率，再用 beam search 一步步找到最可能的路径。
https://t.co/2iVJd983QA

10. jev-desktop
把 Jev 接到桌面自动化里。它读取 Accessibility Tree，判断该操作哪个控件、执行什么动作，再交给本地执行器。
https://t.co/mLGTp4BwXz

11. TypeSafe AI Playground
一个专门拿 Jev 做实验的 Rust CLI，已经做了 PHI 检测、代码注释审查、实时语气分析、职业和行业分类等玩法。
https://t.co/ELLsEZAGMR

12. Prism
目前我看到最接近量化/交易场景的项目。它让 Jev 判断流动性池的 toxic flow、市场压力、均值回归可能性和流动性分布方式，目前默认还是 shadow/advisory，不直接驱动交易。
https://t.co/WqFdwpZilz

13. 1v1 Jev
直接做了一个 FPS，让 Jev 大约 9Hz 判断移动、瞄准、ADS、开枪和跳跃。属于最直观展示 Jev 低延迟决策能力的项目之一。
https://t.co/RpBCFScEey

14. TypeSafe on Neon
拿 Jev 做模型 Router。请求先由 Jev 判断属于哪种任务，再转给 Grok 4.6 或 GPT-6 Astra 等模型执行。
https://t.co/ArCsOwexTM

看完这些项目，你大概也知道 Jev 可以怎么玩了，就是拿它反复做「要不要、选哪个、打几分、下一步干什么」。

真正需要生成代码、写文章和复杂推理时，再把任务交给传统大模型。
author: 0xJackieeee
quoted_text:
前 OpenAI 研究员 Diogo Almeida 创办的 TypeSafe AI 推出新模型 Jev。它有点像一个能读懂自然语言的超级分类器，不生成文本，只返回选项、分数和概率，专门给软件做判断。

普通大模型需要一个 token 一个 token 往外生成，Jev 则可以并行给出多个结果。TypeSafe 还用新的 RLCD 方法训练它的置信度，让模型在给出判断的同时，告诉程序自己有多大把握。

TypeSafe 用安全告警、Agent 审查、发票处理和客服做了 4 组自动化工作流测试。在这套自建评测里，Jev 最高比 Claude Sonnet 5 快约 193.6 倍，比 Claude Opus 5 便宜约 444.6 倍。

TypeSafe 把 Jev 称为首款「System One Model」（快速决策模型），名字来自卡尼曼《思考，快与慢》里的 System 1。它专门处理分类、打分、路由和下一步决策这类快速判断任务。
